target.title: fix(codex): prevent startup hangs after binding migration
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running any OpenClaw CLI command or starting the gateway could experience a long startup stall when Codex app-server binding sidecars had already been imported into SQLite but their session owners could not be resolved.

The migration left those successfully imported files under the legacy discoverable suffix, so every new process recursively found and revalidated all of them. A live affected installation had 5,428 retained sidecars; concurrent CLI and gateway starts repeatedly scanned the same set and contended on their locks.

## Why This Change Was Made

After the canonical conversation binding is registered and verified, the migration now archives the legacy source even when no session owner is available. Invalid bindings, conflicting canonical state, foreign harness ownership, failed owner writes, and archive failures continue to retain the source and report warnings.

This matches the Codex app-server contract: `thread/resume` prefers the durable thread id, which remains in the canonical SQLite conversation binding; the old OpenClaw sidecar is not a Codex runtime input.

## User Impact

Codex binding migration now converges. Successfully imported orphan sidecars no longer trigger the same full migration scan on every CLI or gateway process, preventing startup hangs and repeated migration notices without overwriting conflicting state.

## Evidence

- Regression test updated to prove an unresolved-owner sidecar is imported, archived, absent from subsequent detection, and a second migration is a no-op.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` — 1 file passed, 9 tests passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/codex/doctor-contract-api.test.ts extensions/codex/src/migration/session-binding-sidecars.ts` — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Live recovery proof: all 5,428 retained sources had canonical SQLite rows; after removing the verified legacy sources from the scan path, `openclaw --version` completed in 0.06 seconds and gateway health completed in 11 ms.
- `codex review --base origin/main` was attempted, but the account reached its five-hour rate limit before the review produced a verdict.

AI-assisted: yes. I inspected and understand the migration, canonical binding, and Codex resume paths changed or relied on here.
